Model parameters & references

Lineage of ColE1/pBR322 kinetic-ODE models

Four published kinetic-ODE models describe ColE1-family plasmid replication via the RNA I / RNA II antisense mechanism. Each refines its predecessor; later models add explicit biology (Rom protein, kissing complex, tRNA) at the cost of more parameters. Stochastic / agent-based descendants (e.g. Kuo 1996, Mathur 2009) re-use the same rate constants, so the table below covers the upstream parameter source for the entire family.

What this v2ecoli implementation uses, and why

We integrate the full Brendel & Perelson 1993 (rom+) ODE system — eqns 1a–1j of the paper — as written, with all 10 species and all 18 rate constants from BP Table 1. No QSS reduction, no Rom-free shortcut. The system runs in plasmid_replication.py:_bp_deriv; integration is fixed-step RK4 with n_substeps = 10 per process timestep and non-negative clamping after each substep (plasmid_replication.py:_bp_rk4). The cell-growth dilution term μ in BP's eqns is set to 0 — vEcoli handles volume increase and division externally. Replication initiation events are discretized from the continuous flux k_D · D_p into integer firings via a fractional accumulator (repl_accum) that carries between timesteps; the integer count is exposed to _evolve as n_rna_initiations and gated by replisome-subunit availability.

DecisionChoiceReason
Source paper BP 1993 (over Kim-Shuler 1990) BP's published prediction (28 cpc rom+) sits inside the experimental band (~22–30 cpc). Kim-Shuler's 44–60 cpc is at the high end and uses a 33-s RNA half-life that's a fast-growth artifact. BP's 2-minute half-life matches the field standard.
Source paper BP 1993 (over Freudenau 2015) Freudenau's 26 reactions and 15 species extend BP with uncharged-tRNA binding to RNA II / pDNA-RNA II — a layer BP doesn't need. Their fitted RNA I synthesis rate (k13=34/min, vs BP's 6/min) only makes sense WITH the extra tRNA-buffering reactions that compensate for it. Plugging Freudenau's numbers into BP's structure would over-produce RNA I and crash cpc below BP's 28. Freudenau is the natural Stage B target once the BP backbone is validated.
Strain (rom+ vs rom⁻) rom+ Native pBR322 carries an intact rom gene. Freudenau's reference strain DH5α-pSUP 201-3 is also rom+.
Kissing complex Explicit — DtII, D*c, Dc, DM all tracked separately BP's 1a–1g D-state chain (free → RI-bound short RNA II → elongated → primer → kissing complex with Rom) is integrated directly. Crucially only short RNA II (DtII, 110–360 nt) is RI-susceptible; once elongated past 360 nt to DlII the loop region is no longer accessible. Dropping that distinction (the QSS-on-everything shortcut) under-inhibits and pushes cpc out of the BP target band.
Rom protein Explicit — M tracked, k3·M·D*c stabilizes the kissing complex The rom+ parameter set hinges on this stabilization step. Without it the rom+/rom⁻ distinction collapses and the predicted cpc moves to the rom⁻ value (~52). M dynamics use BP eqn 1j directly.
Cell volume Vc Fixed 0.625 fL (BP convention) BP's M⁻¹·min⁻¹ rates (k1, k3) are coupled to their reported Vc; coupling to v2ecoli's dynamic cell volume (1–2 fL) would dilute RNAs ~3× and crash the steady state. The fixed-Vc choice is temporary — once RNA I/II become bulk molecules transcribed by the main RNAP stack (Stage C, see roadmap), hybridization becomes a count-based reaction and Vc drops out entirely.
Initiation gate Discretized BP flux: integer part of ∫ kD·Dp dt The continuous replication flux is the rate of D → 2 D in BP eqn 1a. We integrate, accumulate the fractional remainder across timesteps, and emit the integer part as discrete initiation events that the chromosome-replication-style modules in plasmid_replication.py consume. No survival-probability approximation needed.

BP 1993 parameter set (rom+) — values used here

All values from BP 1993 Table 1, in the paper's native units (min⁻¹ for unimolecular, M⁻¹·min⁻¹ for bimolecular). Bimolecular rates are converted at runtime to count-based per-second rates via k / (NA·Vc) / 60; unimolecular rates are divided by 60 to become per-second (plasmid_replication.py:initialize). The defaults below are exactly the values in PlasmidReplication.config_schema.

How the model runs inside v2ecoli

The BP1993 ODE lives in v2ecoli/processes/plasmid_replication.py as the PlasmidReplication Step. Each tick it (a) re-syncs the continuous D-pool to the integer full_plasmids count that v2ecoli is tracking, (b) integrates eqns 1a–1j over the tick, and (c) discretizes the continuous replication flux into integer initiation events that create new plasmid replisome unique molecules. The integer-count side of v2ecoli (full_plasmids, plasmid_active_replisomes, oriVs, plasmid_domains) stays authoritative; the ODE is a control signal, not a parallel copy of the plasmid inventory.

The 10-species state machine

Seven D-species are all the same plasmid DNA in different RNA II / RNA I / Rom complexation states. The three free species (RI, RII, M) float in the cytoplasm.

SpeciesMeaningRole in the loop
D Idle plasmid (no RNA II in progress) Reservoir. Re-enters via primer release (kD·Dp), loop re-opening (k−l·DlII) and kissing-complex disassembly (k−c·Dc).
DtII Plasmid with short RNA II transcript (110–360 nt) The control point. Either matures to DlII (rate kl) or is captured by RI into D*c (rate k1·RI).
DlII Plasmid with long RNA II transcript (past 360 nt) Loop region folded away — RI can no longer bind. Commits to primer (kp) or aborts (k−l).
Dp Primer-ready plasmid (RNase H cleaved) One tick at kD and the plasmid replicates (D → 2·D).
D*c Kissing complex (reversible RI·DtII) First committed inhibited state. Feeds Dc (k2) or DM (k3·M).
Dc Stable inhibited complex (cleaved) Dead end except for slow disassembly (k−c) back to D.
DM Rom-stabilized inhibited complex Rom bound to D*c. Hands off to Dc (k4). Carrier of the rom+ phenotype.
RI Free antisense RNA I (inhibitor) Produced at kI·D, degraded at εI. Drives the negative feedback: more plasmids → more RI → more DtII captured before maturation.
RII Free RNA II (aborted transcripts) Not reused; degraded at εII. Released from DlII (k−l) and Dp (kD, at primer cleavage).
M Free Rom protein Produced at kM·D, degraded at εM, binds D*c at k3. No Rom → DM stays empty → rom⁻-like phenotype emerges from the chemistry.

The per-tick handshake with v2ecoli's unique-molecule stack

v2ecoli counts plasmids with an integer full_plasmids unique-molecule array; BP1993's D-pool is continuous. The two are reconciled in _prepare every timestep:

  1. Read the truth. n_plasmids = sum(full_plasmids._entryState) and n_active = sum(plasmid_active_replisomes._entryState). n_idle = n_plasmids − n_active is the number of plasmids available to sit in one of the seven D-states.
  2. Renormalize the D-pool to n_idle. sum(D, DtII, DlII, Dp, D*c, Dc, DM) = n_idle after scaling. Division and replication-termination change n_full_plasmids externally; this step absorbs those jumps without perturbing the species ratios.
  3. Integrate eqns 1a–1j with RK4, n_substeps = 10 per tick, non-negative clamp after each substep (_bp_rk4).
  4. Discretize the replication flux. During integration the 2·kD·Dp term in dD/dt inflates the D-pool above n_idle; the growth Δ = new_sum − n_idle is the continuous number of replication events that should fire this tick. Add Δ into repl_accum and emit n_rna_initiations = int(repl_accum); keep the fractional remainder for next tick. Renormalize the D-pool back to n_idle.
  5. Hand n_rna_initiations to Module 1. In _evolve, Module 1 takes min of the requested initiations, available idle plasmid domains, and subunit-gated max_new_replisomes, then builds that many new plasmid_active_replisome unique molecules and decrements the corresponding subunit bulk counts.

Inputs — what v2ecoli feeds into the process

PortTypeUsed for
bulk bulk molecule array Read: replisome subunits (DnaG, DnaB, HolA, pol III core, β-clamp) to compute max_new_replisomes; dNTPs for polymerization; PPi for by-product accounting.
full_plasmids unique-molecule array Sum gives n_plasmids — the authoritative integer copy number. Pins sum(D-pool) via renormalization.
plasmid_active_replisomes unique-molecule array Sum gives n_active, subtracted from n_plasmids to get n_idle (the D-pool size). Also walked forward by Module 2 at elongation.
oriVs, plasmid_domains unique-molecule arrays Identify which plasmid domains have an active replisome vs. which are idle (idle_plasmid_domains), so Module 1 only initiates on replisome-free domains.
environment.media_id string Routed through to make_elongation_rates so the basal elongation rate can be media-conditioned (inherited from the chromosomal replication process).
plasmid_rna_control 12 scalar fields The ODE's own state (10 species + repl_accum + n_rna_initiations). Read at the start of the tick, overwritten at the end.
timestep, global_time integer[s], float Tick length (1 s for the plasmid loop) and absolute sim time. RK4 integrates over timestep.

Outputs — what the process feeds back to v2ecoli

PortUpdate typeEffect
bulk deltas (subunit draws, dNTP consumption, PPi release) Each new replisome debits one trimer and one monomer set of subunits from bulk; active replisomes consume dNTPs and emit PPi during elongation. This is the coupling that lets plasmid replication compete with chromosomal replication for shared pools — the DnaG depletion signature is visible precisely because of this.
plasmid_active_replisomes adds / moves / terminates unique molecules New replisomes created by Module 1 (one per initiation event). Module 2 advances their coordinates each tick. Module 3 deletes them at termination and spawns daughter full_plasmids.
full_plasmids, plasmid_domains, oriVs adds unique molecules (at replication completion) A completed replisome run produces two daughter plasmids, each with its own oriV and domain entry. This is the only path by which n_full_plasmids grows — the ODE never writes to it directly.
plasmid_rna_control overwrite on all 12 scalar fields Post-integration ODE state (10 species, renormalized), updated repl_accum, and n_rna_initiations for the current tick. This is what the report's §3 & §4 plots read.
listeners.replication_data.plasmid_critical_mass_per_oriV overwrite[float] Reported as 0 when the BP1993 ODE is driving initiation (no critical-mass gate is in use). Kept in the schema so the chromosomal-style listener is still populated.

Boundary contracts worth knowing

  • Integer vs. float responsibility. The ODE never creates or destroys full_plasmids. Every plasmid count change goes through Module 1 (initiation) or Module 3 (termination → daughter), which manipulate the unique-molecule store. The ODE's only lever is n_rna_initiations, which caps how many Module 1 attempts per tick.
  • Dilution handled externally (μ = 0). BP 1993's eqns include a −μ·species term for growth dilution; here it's dropped because v2ecoli's composite halves every species at cell division via divide_cell rather than shrinking continuously.
  • Fixed Vc = 0.625 fL. BP's bimolecular rates (k1, k3) are reported in M⁻¹·min⁻¹ against BP's declared cell volume. Coupling them to v2ecoli's dynamic 1–2 fL would implicitly rescale every hybridization rate over the cell cycle and destabilize the steady state. Removing this boundary is a Stage C roadmap item.
  • RI, RII, M stay inside plasmid_rna_control. They are not bulk molecules, not transcribed by the main RNAP stack, and not mass-accounted. Stage C promotes RNA I/II to proper bulk species driven by the whole-cell transcription process — then hybridization becomes a standard count-based reaction and the fixed-Vc caveat drops out.
  • No direct oriV → replication call. The oriV unique molecule is purely a locus marker used for bookkeeping (Module 1 finds idle domains, Module 3 distributes oriVs to daughters). The ODE decides whether to initiate; the oriV tells Module 1 where on the plasmid to place the new replisome.

What changed vs. the prior 3-ODE QSS implementation

v2ecoli previously ran a QSS-reduced version of the BP1993 chemistry: 3 species (RNA I, RNA II, hybrid), single bimolecular hybridization with keff = k1·k2/(k−1+k2) absorbing the kissing-complex chemistry, and a Kim-Shuler-style exp(−kh·RI·τ) survival-probability gate on initiation. The reduction was algebraically clean but produced multigen drift away from BP's predicted 28 cpc and could not distinguish rom+ from rom⁻. The current implementation runs the full BP1993 ODE.

AspectPrior (3-ODE QSS) Current (full BP1993)Why the change
Species count 3 (RI, RII, hybrid) 10 (D, DtII, DlII, Dp, D*c, Dc, DM, RI, RII, M) The D-state chain (per-plasmid replication-cycle position) and the explicit Rom dimer M are what carry the rom+/rom⁻ distinction.
Kissing complex Folded into keff via QSS Explicit reversible D*c; explicit cleaved Dc and Rom-stabilized DM QSS assumes d D*c/dt = 0, which only holds when k−1+k2 ≫ all surrounding fluxes; under depletion of RI at low cpc it doesn't.
RI susceptibility All RNA II RI-susceptible (single hybrid pool) Only short RNA II (DtII, 110–360 nt) is RI-susceptible; DlII is past the inhibition window BP §2 makes this explicit (eqns 1b vs 1c). Lumping DlII into the inhibitable pool over-inhibits and pushes cpc down.
Rom protein Implicit in the "rom+" parameter values (no M dynamics) Explicit M synthesis (kM·D), degradation (εM·M), and binding to D*c (k3) Required for rom+ vs rom⁻ to come from the chemistry rather than a magic constant; matches BP eqn 1j directly.
Replication initiation Kim-Shuler 1990 Eq 6 survival probability exp(−kh·RI·τ) gate Discretized BP flux: integer part of ∫ kD·Dp dt per timestep, fractional remainder accumulated in repl_accum The KS Eq 6 gate is a closed-form approximation of BP's kl/kp primer-vs-loop competition; integrating BP's eqn 1d directly removes the approximation and exposes the fractional-event accounting to the reader as n_rna_initiations.
Integration Closed-form QSS update per timestep Fixed-step RK4, n_substeps = 10 per process timestep, with non-negative clamping RK4 handles the stiff RI·DtII coupling cleanly; clamping prevents transient negatives from biting later substeps.
Vcfixed 0.625 fL (BP convention) fixed 0.625 fL (BP convention) — unchanged Same constraint: BP's M⁻¹·min⁻¹ rates only cohere with their Vc. Drops out at Stage C when hybridization becomes count-based.
Predicted cpc (rom+) drift away from 28 cpc across multigen lineage ~28 cpc (matches BP Table 2 — see §8 lineage) The headline. The full-ODE behaviour reproduces BP's published rom+ prediction; Stage B (Freudenau 2015) extends to 46–49 cpc.

References

  • Brendel & Perelson 1993 — J. Mol. Biol. 229:860. Kinetic model of ColE1 plasmid replication control with explicit kissing complex and Rom regulation. Table 1 lists all rate constants; Table 2 predicts 28 cpc for rom+ wild-type, 52 cpc rom⁻. Primary source for the current parameter set.
  • Freudenau et al. 2015 — Front. Bioeng. Biotechnol. 3:127. Extends BP 1993 with explicit Rom and uncharged-tRNA dynamics; refits 26 rate constants to qPCR-measured RNAI/RNAII/PCN on DH5α-pSUP 201-3 (low-copy pBR322 derivative). Reports 46–49 cpc across three timepoints. Stage B target.
  • Kim & Shuler 1990 — Biotechnol. Bioeng. 36:233. pBR322 in B/r at 0.08–0.84 h⁻¹. Replaced as the parameter source but Eq 6 (RNA-II initiation survival probability exp(−kh·RNAI·τ)) is still the gate we use.
  • Ataai & Shuler 1986 — Biotechnol. Bioeng. 28:1166. Original three-ODE framework for RNA-I/II/hybrid that BP refines.

Deferred (roadmap)

  • Stage B — explicit Rom dynamics (Freudenau et al. 2015). Add Rom protein synthesis/degradation and the Rom·Cm ⇌ Rom·Cs stabilization step. This raises the effective hybridization rate ~1.6× and lifts predicted cpc from BP's 28 → Freudenau's measured 46–49.
  • Stage C — mechanistic RNA I / RNA II transcription (architectural target). Today the BP1993 10-species pool (D-chain, RI, RII, M) lives as scalars in process_state.plasmid_rna_control, and division requires bespoke halving logic in library/division.py. The end-state is to make RI and RII actual bulk molecules produced by the standard ecoli-transcript-initiation + ecoli-transcript-elongation processes firing off plasmid promoters, with the kissing-complex chemistry running as count-based reactions on those bulk pools. At that point the custom process-state halving becomes dead code, Vc drops out (count-based reaction), and the BP D-state chain reduces to bookkeeping over which plasmid copies are currently engaged with bulk RNA II / Rom — see project memory plasmid_mechanistic_target.
  • Growth-rate dependence of αI / αII, stochastic RNA II initiation (Poisson over the 240 s window), segregational loss at low copy, ppGpp linkage, multimer recombination, metabolic burden — stages D–G.

LexA is the dominant TF on EG10239_RNA (dnaG). It's classified as 0CS in v2ecoli (no DNA-damage activation path), so it sits near-saturated on all 53 targets for the whole run.

8. Chromosome dynamics — multigeneration lineage

Single-lineage run through a plasmid-enabled cache: start from the baseline newborn, run to division, keep daughter 1, rebuild a fresh Composite, repeat. Ran 8/8 generations in 1863s wall. Snapshot interval: 1s. All figures below are on one cumulative time axis — dashed vertical lines are generation boundaries.

Lineage summary: 8/8 generations divided · peak full_plasmid count 28, end-of-lineage 26 · copy-number trajectory hit the BP1993 Table 2 target band (≥26 cpc) at gen 6.

Not the mechanistic implementation. This run uses the BP1993 reduced ODE living in process_state.plasmid_rna_control (10 lumped species: D-pool, RI, RII, M). RNA I and RNA II are not bulk molecules transcribed by the main RNAP stack; the ODE substitutes for the full transcription/degradation chemistry. Replication firing is discretized from the ODE flux into integer events. The mechanistic target — RNA I/II as bulk molecules going through transcription + degradation like every other v2ecoli RNA — is the next stage; see the parameters section above for the staging rationale.
